newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS adopts acronym as world brand name.
newsitem.headline: UBS adopts acronym as world brand name.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland said it was adopting the acronym UBS as a global brand rather than spelling out its full name or using its German-language name as it has traditionally done in Switzerland.
UBS is the second of Switzerland's three big banks to change its brand name after CS Holding this year reorganised as Credit Suisse Group.
Chief executive Mathis Cabiallavetta said the change was part of UBS's strategy of becoming increasingly global.
"In today's world, strong, uniform brands are improtant not only in the consumer goods sector," Cabiallavetta told a news conference.
"They are playing an increasingly significant role in the service sector, and there is a proven link between a strong brand and the strength of an organisation," he added.
The brand will be the acronym UBS in large, bold red letters above the name Union Bank of Switzerland in much smaller black letters.
The change will take effect on May 1, when the name on its flagship buildings in Switzerland and abroad will be changed.
This includes dropping the traditional German name Schweizerische Bankgesellschaft and acronym SBG used in the company's homeland of German-speaking Switzerland.

UBS is following a trend set by Credit Suisse Group when it standardised its global brand as of January 1, including dropping a German name widely used in Switzerland. Its two banks groups are now called Credit Suisse and Credit Suisse First Boston.
